name: Baryon-to-photon ratio from BBN deuterium
summary: Baryogenesis must produce the eta_B that BBN measures from the primordial D/H ratio (and the CMB confirms); BBN is the earliest direct test of any baryogenesis model.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

Sakharov (1967). "Violation of CP invariance, C asymmetry, and baryon asymmetry of the universe". *Sov. Phys. Usp.* 34, 392. [doi:10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497](https://doi.org/10.1070/PU1991v034n05ABEH002497)

name: Same stopping-power physics and detector technologies
summary: Bethe-Bloch energy loss, scintillators, gas counters and silicon sensors are common to collider detectors and nuclear radiation detection; HEP trackers and calorimeters descend from nuclear counters and feed back into dosimetry instruments.
sources: Particle Data Group (2024). "Review of Particle Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 110, 030001. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001)

name: Neutrino decoupling, N_eff and n/p freeze-out
summary: Weak n<->p conversions with neutrinos freeze out at T~0.8 MeV and set Y_p; the number of light neutrino species (N_eff) changes the expansion rate and hence the helium yield.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Pauli's neutrino and Fermi's beta decay
summary: The neutrino was invented to save energy conservation in beta decay and first detected via inverse beta decay at a reactor; beta spectra remain the key laboratory window on neutrino properties.
sources: Fermi (1934). "Versuch einer Theorie der β-Strahlen. I". *Z. Phys.* 88, 161. [doi:10.1007/BF01351864](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01351864)
Cowan, Reines et al. (1956). "Detection of the Free Neutrino: a Confirmation". *Science* 124, 103. [doi:10.1126/science.124.3212.103](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.124.3212.103)

name: Tritium endpoint and double-beta decay
summary: Absolute neutrino mass comes from the shape of the tritium beta spectrum near its endpoint (KATRIN), and Majorana nature from nuclear 0nubb decay; both are nuclear weak decays read as neutrino measurements.
sources: KATRIN Collaboration (2022). "Direct neutrino-mass measurement with sub-electronvolt sensitivity". *Nature Phys.* 18, 160. [arXiv:2105.08533](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.08533)
Avignone, Elliott & Engel (2008). "Double Beta Decay, Majorana Neutrinos, and Neutrino Mass". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 481. [arXiv:0708.1033](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1033)

name: Chiral EFT as Weinberg's power counting for nuclei
summary: Weinberg's phenomenological-Lagrangian program (chiral perturbation theory) was carried into nuclear physics as chiral EFT, organizing nucleon-nucleon and three-nucleon forces in powers of Q/Lambda_chi.
sources: Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)
Weinberg (1990). "Nuclear forces from chiral lagrangians". *Phys. Lett. B* 251, 288. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3)
Epelbaum, Hammer & Meißner (2009). "Modern theory of nuclear forces". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1773. [arXiv:0811.1338](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1338)

name: Lattice QCD finds the crossover at T_c~156 MeV
summary: Euclidean lattice Monte Carlo establishes that the physical-mass QCD transition at mu_B=0 is a crossover and computes the equation of state and susceptibilities used to search for a critical point; the sign problem blocks large mu_B.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)
Borsanyi et al. (2010). "Is there still any T_c mystery in lattice QCD? Results with physical masses in the continuum limit III". *JHEP* 09, 073. [arXiv:1005.3508](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3508)

name: Fermi contact theory as low-energy W exchange
summary: Fermi's four-fermion interaction is the q^2<<m_W^2 limit of W exchange in SU(2)xU(1); maximal parity violation seen in 60Co decay fixed the V-A, left-handed structure of the electroweak theory.
sources: Fermi (1934). "Versuch einer Theorie der β-Strahlen. I". *Z. Phys.* 88, 161. [doi:10.1007/BF01351864](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01351864)

name: DGLAP evolution of parton distributions
summary: PDFs are non-perturbative proton matrix elements whose scale dependence is fixed by perturbative QCD splitting functions; Bjorken scaling and its logarithmic violation are asymptotic freedom seen in DIS.
sources: Altarelli & Parisi (1977). "Asymptotic freedom in parton language". *Nucl. Phys. B* 126, 298. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4)
Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)

name: Asymptotic freedom implies deconfined matter
summary: Because alpha_s runs to zero at high momentum scales, hot or dense QCD matter deconfines into a quark-gluon plasma; its Stefan-Boltzmann limit counts gluon and quark degrees of freedom.
sources: Collins & Perry (1975). "Superdense Matter: Neutrons or Asymptotically Free Quarks?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 34, 1353. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1353](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1353)
Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)

name: Shared radiation-detector toolkit
summary: Applied nuclear physics (reactor instrumentation, dosimetry, isotope assay) and collider experiments use the same detector families and the same interaction physics; technology flows both ways.
sources: Particle Data Group (2024). "Review of Particle Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 110, 030001. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001)

name: Proton structure as input to every LHC cross section
summary: LHC rates factorize into partonic cross sections convolved with PDFs measured in DIS; PDF uncertainties now limit precision Higgs and W-mass measurements.
sources: NNPDF Collaboration (2015). "Parton distributions for the LHC Run II". *JHEP* 04, 040. [arXiv:1410.8849](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.8849)

name: Nucleon structure is non-perturbative QCD
summary: The proton's parton content, spin and mass are QCD bound-state properties; nuclear-physics DIS experiments supplied the evidence for quarks and asymptotic freedom.
sources: Altarelli & Parisi (1977). "Asymptotic freedom in parton language". *Nucl. Phys. B* 126, 298. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4)

name: Next QCD collider after HERA and the LHC
summary: The EIC extends HERA's ep programme to polarized and nuclear beams; its small-x gluon and nuclear PDF measurements feed LHC and heavy-ion predictions, and it reuses collider accelerator and detector technology.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: Proton radius puzzle as a precision anomaly
summary: The muonic-hydrogen proton radius disagreed with e-p data by ~5 sigma, a case study for judging precision anomalies (now largely resolved toward 0.84 fm); hadronic structure also limits the muon g-2 prediction.
sources: Pohl et al. (2010). "The size of the proton". *Nature* 466, 213. [doi:10.1038/nature09250](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09250)
Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: DGLAP kernels are parton-shower kernels
summary: The splitting functions P(z) that evolve PDFs in ln mu^2 are the same kernels that generate collinear emissions in parton showers and jet evolution (space-like vs time-like evolution).
sources: Altarelli & Parisi (1977). "Asymptotic freedom in parton language". *Nucl. Phys. B* 126, 298. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4)
Sjöstrand et al. (2015). "An introduction to PYTHIA 8.2". *Comput. Phys. Commun.* 191, 159. [arXiv:1410.3012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3012)

name: Heavy-ion collisions map QCD matter
summary: Heavy-ion programmes at RHIC and the LHC study QCD at high temperature and density: deconfinement, chiral restoration, collective flow and jet quenching.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

name: Jets as tomographic probes of the QGP
summary: IRC-safe jet algorithms, substructure and grooming developed for pp physics are applied in PbPb collisions; medium-induced radiation modifies the vacuum shower and the pp jets serve as the baseline for R_AA.
sources: Cacciari, Salam & Soyez (2008). "The anti-k_t jet clustering algorithm". *JHEP* 04, 063. [arXiv:0802.1189](https://arxiv.org/abs/0802.1189)

name: Nuclear weak decays as flavor probes
summary: Nuclear beta decays supply the most precise CKM element |V_ud| and tests of first-row unitarity, which constrains new physics at the 10^-4 level.
sources: Hardy & Towner (2020). "Superallowed 0+→0+ nuclear β decays: 2020 critical survey, with implications for Vud and CKM unitarity". *Phys. Rev. C* 102, 045501. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501)

name: EFT organizes the nuclear many-body problem
summary: Nuclear structure theory is now built from a hierarchy of EFTs (chiral, pionless, halo), each with power counting and quantified truncation errors, as in particle-physics EFT.
sources: Hammer, König & van Kolck (2020). "Nuclear effective field theory: status and perspectives". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 92, 025004. [arXiv:1906.12122](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.12122)

name: Lattice QCD computes nucleon-nucleon interactions
summary: Lattice QCD extracts two-baryon scattering from finite-volume energy levels (Luscher's method) and fixes chiral-EFT low-energy constants, connecting nuclear forces to QCD.
sources: Beane, Detmold, Orginos & Savage (2011). "Nuclear Physics from Lattice QCD". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 66, 1. [arXiv:1004.2935](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2935)

name: Pions as pseudo-Goldstone bosons mediate nuclear force
summary: Spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking in QCD makes the pion light; its exchange is the long-range part of the nuclear force (Yukawa), with pion couplings fixed by chiral symmetry (Goldberger-Treiman).
sources: Weinberg (1990). "Nuclear forces from chiral lagrangians". *Phys. Lett. B* 251, 288. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3)
Epelbaum, Hammer & Meißner (2009). "Modern theory of nuclear forces". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1773. [arXiv:0811.1338](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1338)

name: Axial anomaly in the proton spin puzzle
summary: The flavor-singlet axial current is anomalous, so the quark-spin fraction Delta Sigma measured in polarized DIS mixes with gluon polarization; this anomaly is central to interpreting the EMC spin crisis.
sources: European Muon Collaboration (1988). "A measurement of the spin asymmetry and determination of the structure function g1 in deep inelastic muon-proton scattering". *Phys. Lett. B* 206, 364. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7)
Minamiguchi & Uji (2026). "Chiral anomaly and nucleon spin decomposition in the chiral quark soliton model". [arXiv:2609.25867](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25867)

name: SRG/IMSRG as Wilsonian RG for nuclei
summary: Similarity renormalization group evolution decouples high- and low-momentum modes of nuclear Hamiltonians, the nuclear realization of Wilson's integrating-out; induced many-body forces play the role of generated irrelevant operators.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)
Bogner, Furnstahl & Schwenk (2010). "From low-momentum interactions to nuclear structure". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 65, 94. [arXiv:0912.3688](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.3688)
He & Stroberg (2024). "Factorized approximation to the in-medium similarity renormalization group IMSRG(3)". [arXiv:2405.19594](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19594)

name: Nuclear lattice EFT reuses lattice Monte Carlo
summary: Nuclear lattice EFT discretizes chiral-EFT nucleons on a Euclidean space-time lattice and samples auxiliary fields by Monte Carlo, inheriting lattice-QCD algorithms and the fermion sign problem.
sources: Lee (2009). "Lattice simulations for few- and many-body systems". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 63, 117. [arXiv:0804.3501](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.3501)

name: Phases of QCD at finite T and mu_B
summary: QCD's chiral and center symmetries organize its phase diagram: chiral restoration and deconfinement at high T, a conjectured critical point, and color-superconducting (CFL) phases at high density.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)
Alford, Rajagopal & Wilczek (1999). "Color-flavor locking and chiral symmetry breaking in high density QCD". *Nucl. Phys. B* 537, 443. [arXiv:hep-ph/9804403](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9804403)
Du et al. (2025). "The QCD phase diagram and Beam Energy Scan physics: A theory overview". [arXiv:2402.10183](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10183)

name: Conformal plasmas as QGP benchmarks
summary: Strongly coupled conformal plasmas (N=4 SYM via holography) give eta/s=1/4pi, close to the QGP value; QCD's trace anomaly (epsilon-3P)/T^4 measures how far the real plasma is from conformal.
breaks: N=4 SYM is supersymmetric, conformal and large-N with no confinement, no chiral symmetry breaking and no running coupling; QCD is strongly non-conformal near T_c.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)
Boyd et al. (1996). "Thermodynamics of SU(3) lattice gauge theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 469, 419. [arXiv:hep-lat/9602007](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/9602007)

name: Quenching models built on vacuum parton showers
summary: Jet-quenching Monte Carlos (JEWEL, MARTINI, JETSCAPE) embed PYTHIA-type showers in an evolving medium, adding medium-induced splittings and recoils to the Sudakov evolution.
sources: Sjöstrand et al. (2015). "An introduction to PYTHIA 8.2". *Comput. Phys. Commun.* 191, 159. [arXiv:1410.3012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3012)

name: Collectivity and hadronization in small systems
summary: High-multiplicity pp collisions show flow-like correlations and strangeness enhancement once thought unique to nuclear collisions; event generators add core-corona or rope hadronization to describe them.
sources: Pierog et al. (2015). "EPOS LHC: Test of collective hadronization with data measured at the CERN Large Hadron Collider". *Phys. Rev. C* 92, 034906. [arXiv:1306.0121](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0121)
ALICE Collaboration (2017). "Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions". *Nature Phys.* 13, 535. [arXiv:1606.07424](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07424)

name: Near-threshold exotics as deuteron-like molecules
summary: States such as X(3872) and T_cc+ lie just below two-hadron thresholds, so the same universal shallow-bound-state physics and Weinberg compositeness criterion used for the deuteron applies; meson-exchange forces bind them.
sources: Weinberg (1965). "Evidence That the Deuteron Is Not an Elementary Particle". *Phys. Rev.* 137, B672. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.137.B672](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.137.B672)
LHCb Collaboration (2022). "Observation of an exotic narrow doubly charmed tetraquark". *Nature Phys.* 18, 751. [arXiv:2109.01038](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.01038)

name: Spin crisis exposes the constituent quark model
summary: The static quark model that organizes baryon multiplets predicts quarks carry essentially all the proton spin; the EMC result Delta Sigma ~ 0.3 showed that sea quarks, gluons and orbital motion matter.
sources: European Muon Collaboration (1988). "A measurement of the spin asymmetry and determination of the structure function g1 in deep inelastic muon-proton scattering". *Phys. Lett. B* 206, 364. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7)
Ji (1997). "Gauge-Invariant Decomposition of Nucleon Spin". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 78, 610. [arXiv:hep-ph/9603249](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9603249)

name: Gluon saturation and the origin of nucleon mass
summary: Non-linear QCD evolution predicts gluon densities saturate at small x (color glass condensate), and the trace anomaly makes most of the nucleon mass gluonic; both are EIC flagship measurements.
sources: Gelis, Iancu, Jalilian-Marian & Venugopalan (2010). "The Color Glass Condensate". *Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 60, 463. [arXiv:1002.0333](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0333)
Ji (1995). "QCD analysis of the mass structure of the nucleon". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 74, 1071. [arXiv:hep-ph/9410274](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9410274)
Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: Topology and U(1)_A at the QCD transition
summary: Instanton-induced U(1)_A breaking controls the order of the chiral transition, the topological susceptibility sets the temperature-dependent axion mass, and sphaleron-driven chirality imbalance motivates chiral-magnetic-effect searches.
sources: Pisarski & Rennecke (2024). "Conjectures about the Chiral Phase Transition in QCD from Anomalous Multi-Instanton Interactions". [arXiv:2401.06130](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06130)
Fukushima, Kharzeev & Warringa (2008). "The Chiral Magnetic Effect". *Phys. Rev. D* 78, 074033. [arXiv:0808.3382](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.3382)

name: Axion emission from nucleon bremsstrahlung
summary: Axion bounds from SN 1987A and neutron-star cooling rest on nuclear physics: NN bremsstrahlung rates, dense-matter EOS and superfluid gaps set how fast axions drain energy from hot nuclear matter.
sources: Caputo & Raffelt (2024). "Astrophysical Axion Bounds: The 2024 Edition". [arXiv:2401.13728](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.13728)

name: Nuclear structure factors for WIMP scattering
summary: Spin-dependent WIMP-nucleus cross sections need the proton and neutron spin content of each target nucleus, computed with the shell model; spin-independent rates need nuclear form factors and the coherent A^2 enhancement.
sources: Goodman & Witten (1985). "Detectability of Certain Dark Matter Candidates". *Phys. Rev. D* 31, 3059. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.31.3059](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.31.3059)

name: Reactors as the strongest terrestrial antineutrino source
summary: Fission-fragment beta decays make ~6 antineutrinos per fission (~2x10^20 per second per GW_th); reactors gave the first neutrino detection, theta_13 (Daya Bay) and the JUNO ordering programme, and allow reactor monitoring.
sources: Cowan, Reines et al. (1956). "Detection of the Free Neutrino: a Confirmation". *Science* 124, 103. [doi:10.1126/science.124.3212.103](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.124.3212.103)
Daya Bay Collaboration (2012). "Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 171803. [arXiv:1203.1669](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1669)

name: Reactor anomaly traced to fission beta spectra
summary: The reactor antineutrino anomaly came from converted fission beta spectra (Huber-Mueller); improved nuclear data and summation calculations removed much of it, and the 5 MeV bump is a nuclear-data feature, not oscillation.
sources: Mention et al. (2011). "The Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly". *Phys. Rev. D* 83, 073006. [arXiv:1101.2755](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2755)
Huber (2011). "On the determination of anti-neutrino spectra from nuclear reactors". *Phys. Rev. C* 84, 024617. [arXiv:1106.0687](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0687)

name: Neutrino flavor conversion sets Y_e in r-process sites
summary: In supernovae and merger remnants, nu_e and anti-nu_e captures on nucleons set the electron fraction Y_e of ejecta; collective and fast flavor conversions can shift Y_e and so the r-process yields.
sources: Duan, Fuller & Qian (2010). "Collective Neutrino Oscillations". *Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 60, 569. [arXiv:1001.2799](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2799)

Arnould, Goriely & Takahashi (2007). "The r-process of stellar nucleosynthesis: Astrophysics and nuclear physics achievements and mysteries". *Phys. Rep.* 450, 97. [arXiv:0705.4512](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4512)

name: Solar neutrinos measure pp-chain and CNO rates
summary: Solar neutrino fluxes are predicted from fusion S-factors (pp, 7Be(p,gamma)8B, 3He+4He) and measured by Borexino, SNO and Super-K, including the first CNO neutrinos; they test solar fusion and oscillations together.
sources: Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)
Borexino Collaboration (2020). "Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun". *Nature* 587, 577. [arXiv:2006.15115](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15115)

name: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections and CEvNS
summary: Accelerator oscillation measurements are limited by neutrino-nucleus interaction models (quasi-elastic, meson production, final-state interactions); coherent elastic scattering grows as N^2 through the nuclear weak charge.
sources: Akimov et al. (2017). "Observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering". *Science* 357, 1123. [arXiv:1708.01294](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01294)
Abe et al. (2026). "Constraining Neutrino Interaction Uncertainties for Neutrino Oscillation Measurements at the T2K Experiment". [arXiv:2606.14015](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14015)

name: Ab initio 0nubb matrix elements with uncertainties
summary: Turning a 0nubb half-life limit into m_bb needs |M^0nu|, which shell-model, QRPA and EDF calculations disagree on by 2-3x; ab initio methods with chiral EFT now give matrix elements with error bars, and two-body currents explain g_A quenching.

Belley et al. (2024). "Ab initio Uncertainty Quantification of Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay in Ge76". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 182502. [arXiv:2308.15634](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.15634)
Gysbers et al. (2019). "Discrepancy between experimental and theoretical β-decay rates resolved from first principles". *Nature Phys.* 15, 428. [arXiv:1903.00047](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.00047)

name: Z-boson exchange measures the neutron skin
summary: Parity-violating electron scattering couples to the weak charge, which is carried mostly by neutrons (Q_W^p ~ 1-4 sin^2 theta_W ~ 0.07); PREX-II's 208Pb neutron skin constrains the symmetry-energy slope L and neutron-star radii.
sources: PREX Collaboration (2021). "Accurate Determination of the Neutron Skin Thickness of 208Pb through Parity-Violation in Electron Scattering". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 126, 172502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.126.172502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.126.172502)

name: Neutron EDM as the observable of theta
summary: The theta term is a P- and T-odd topological term that induces a neutron electric dipole moment; the measured bound gives |theta| < 10^-10, the strong-CP problem the axion solves.
sources: Crewther, Di Vecchia, Veneziano & Witten (1979). "Chiral Estimate of the Electric Dipole Moment of the Neutron in Quantum Chromodynamics". *Phys. Lett. B* 88, 123. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(79)90128-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(79)90128-X)
Abel et al. (2020). "Measurement of the Permanent Electric Dipole Moment of the Neutron". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 081803. [arXiv:2001.11966](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.11966)

name: Octupole-deformed nuclei amplify T violation
summary: Nuclear Schiff moments induced by CP-odd nucleon interactions are enhanced by orders of magnitude in octupole-deformed nuclei with parity doublets (225Ra, 227Ac), making atomic EDM searches sensitive probes of hadronic CP violation.

name: Both Standard Model transitions are crossovers
summary: Lattice studies show that at physical masses the electroweak transition (m_h=125 GeV) and the QCD transition are both smooth crossovers, which removes the SM's own departure from equilibrium for baryogenesis and for primordial relics.
sources: Kajantie, Laine, Rummukainen & Shaposhnikov (1996). "Is there a hot electroweak phase transition at m_H ≳ m_W?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 77, 2887. [arXiv:hep-ph/9605288](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9605288)

Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

name: V_ud and first-row CKM unitarity
summary: Superallowed 0+->0+ ft values give |V_ud| = 0.9737; with |V_us| from kaons the first-row sum falls ~3 sigma short of 1 (Cabibbo angle anomaly), sensitive to the gamma-W box radiative correction.
sources: Hardy & Towner (2020). "Superallowed 0+→0+ nuclear β decays: 2020 critical survey, with implications for Vud and CKM unitarity". *Phys. Rev. C* 102, 045501. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.102.045501)
Seng et al. (2018). "Reduced Hadronic Uncertainty in the Determination of V_ud". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 241804. [arXiv:1807.10197](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.10197)

name: Neutron lifetime beam-bottle discrepancy
summary: Beam (~888 s) and bottle (~878 s) neutron lifetimes disagree by ~4 sigma; proposed dark decay channels are tested like other precision anomalies, and the lifetime also feeds BBN and V_ud.
sources: Fornal & Grinstein (2018). "Dark Matter Interpretation of the Neutron Decay Anomaly". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 191801. [arXiv:1801.01124](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.01124)

name: BBN as a probe of BSM physics
summary: Light-element abundances constrain extra relativistic species (N_eff), late-decaying particles, MeV-scale thermal dark matter and time-varying constants; BBN is the earliest laboratory for new physics.
sources: Sarkar (1996). "Big bang nucleosynthesis and physics beyond the standard model". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 59, 1493. [arXiv:hep-ph/9602260](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9602260)
Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Nuclear transitions as dark-boson searches
summary: Excited-nucleus decays via internal pair creation can reveal light bosons; the ATOMKI 8Be/4He anomaly ('X17', ~17 MeV) prompted protophobic dark-photon models but is unconfirmed and contested (MEG II found no signal).
sources: Krasznahorkay et al. (2016). "Observation of Anomalous Internal Pair Creation in 8Be: A Possible Indication of a Light, Neutral Boson". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 042501. [arXiv:1504.01527](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.01527)

name: Hyperon puzzle in neutron-star cores
summary: SU(3) flavor predicts Lambda and Sigma hyperons appear at 2-3 n_0, softening the EOS below what 2 M_sun pulsars allow; hyperon-nucleon and three-baryon forces are the proposed resolution.
sources: Miyatsu et al. (2025). "Equation of State for Hyperonic Neutron-Star Matter in SU(3) Flavor Symmetry". *Symmetry* 17, 1872. [arXiv:2509.16559](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.16559)
Demorest et al. (2010). "A two-solar-mass neutron star measured using Shapiro delay". *Nature* 467, 1081. [doi:10.1038/nature09466](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09466)

name: Quark matter and pQCD constraints on dense EOS
summary: At asymptotic density perturbative QCD fixes the pressure; interpolating between chiral EFT at n_0 and pQCD at ~40 n_0 under causality constrains the neutron-star EOS and suggests quark-matter cores in massive stars.
sources: Annala et al. (2020). "Evidence for quark-matter cores in massive neutron stars". *Nature Phys.* 16, 907. [arXiv:1903.09121](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.09121)

name: Lattice QCD for g_A, spin and gravitational form factors
summary: Lattice QCD computes the nucleon axial charge, quark and gluon spin and orbital contributions, and gravitational form factors (pressure and shear distributions) from first principles.
sources: Hackett et al. (2024). "Gravitational Form Factors of the Proton from Lattice QCD". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 251904. [arXiv:2310.08484](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08484)

name: Large-momentum effective theory puts PDFs on the lattice
summary: Light-cone PDFs cannot be computed in Euclidean time, but equal-time quasi-PDFs in a highly boosted nucleon can, and are matched to PDFs perturbatively (LaMET); lattice results now complement global fits.
sources: Ji (2013). "Parton Physics on a Euclidean Lattice". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 110, 262002. [arXiv:1305.1539](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.1539)

name: Lattice equation of state drives QGP hydrodynamics
summary: Lattice QCD thermodynamics provides the QGP equation of state, speed of sound and trace anomaly used as input to relativistic hydrodynamic simulations of heavy-ion collisions.
sources: Boyd et al. (1996). "Thermodynamics of SU(3) lattice gauge theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 469, 419. [arXiv:hep-lat/9602007](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/9602007)
Borsanyi et al. (2010). "Is there still any T_c mystery in lattice QCD? Results with physical masses in the continuum limit III". *JHEP* 09, 073. [arXiv:1005.3508](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3508)

name: Baryons as Skyrmions
summary: In the large-N chiral Lagrangian, baryons are topological solitons whose winding number is baryon number (the Wess-Zumino-Witten term fixes their fermionic statistics); Skyrmion models describe nucleons and light nuclei.
sources: Skyrme (1962). "A unified field theory of mesons and baryons". *Nucl. Phys.* 31, 556. [doi:10.1016/0029-5582(62)90775-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(62)90775-7)
Witten (1983). "Current algebra, baryons, and quark confinement". *Nucl. Phys. B* 223, 433. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(83)90064-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(83)90064-0)

name: Halo EFT and universality of weak binding
summary: Halo nuclei near the drip lines have a separation energy far below the core excitation scale, so a halo EFT with the core as a point particle applies, with universal (Efimov-like) features for two-neutron halos.
sources: Bedaque & van Kolck (2002). "Effective field theory for few-nucleon systems". *Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 52, 339. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203055](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203055)
Hammer, König & van Kolck (2020). "Nuclear effective field theory: status and perspectives". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 92, 025004. [arXiv:1906.12122](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.12122)

name: Quarkonium melting by color Debye screening
summary: Quarkonia are bound by the Cornell potential; in a QGP color screening shortens its range so states melt sequentially (psi', J/psi, Upsilon), making quarkonium spectra a QGP thermometer.
sources: Matsui & Satz (1986). "J/ψ suppression by quark-gluon plasma formation". *Phys. Lett. B* 178, 416. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8)

name: Geant4 transport for detectors and dose
summary: Geant4, built for HEP detector simulation, is a standard transport code for nuclear detector response and dosimetry, sharing the same cross-section libraries and showering physics.
sources: Agostinelli et al. (2003). "GEANT4—a simulation toolkit". *Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A* 506, 250. [doi:10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8)

name: Many-body field theory: one language for both
summary: Propagators, Feynman diagrams, Matsubara sums, path integrals and the RG moved from particle QFT into many-body theory (Green's functions, Fermi liquids, Hubbard-Stratonovich), and emergent gauge theories flow back.
sources: Georges, Kotliar, Krauth & Rozenberg (1996). "Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated fermion systems and the limit of infinite dimensions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 68, 13. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13)

name: Theta term and axion electrodynamics of 3D TIs
summary: The electromagnetic response of a time-reversal-invariant 3D topological insulator is a theta term with theta=pi, the same topological term as QCD's theta and the axion coupling; it implies a half-quantized surface Hall effect and the Witten effect.
map: \mathcal L_\theta=\frac{\theta e^2}{2\pi h}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B=\frac{\theta\alpha}{4\pi^2}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B,\ \theta=\pi;\ \sigma_{xy}^{\text{surf}}=\tfrac12\tfrac{e^2}{h}
sources: Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)

name: Higgs mechanism first appeared as the Meissner effect
summary: The idea that a condensate gives a gauge field mass migrated from superconductivity (London, Nambu, Anderson) to the Standard Model's electroweak sector.
sources: Nambu (1960). "Quasi-Particles and Gauge Invariance in the Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 117, 648. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.117.648](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.117.648)
Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: Anderson-Higgs mechanism: photon mass = W mass
summary: A superconductor's Cooper-pair condensate eats the phase Goldstone mode and gives the photon a mass 1/lambda_L (Meissner effect), the same abelian Higgs mechanism that gives W and Z masses from the Higgs vev.
map: m_\gamma c^2=\frac{\hbar c}{\lambda_L},\ \lambda_L^{-2}=\mu_0n_se^2/m\ \leftrightarrow\ m_W=\tfrac12gv;\ \Delta\leftrightarrow\langle H\rangle,\ 2e\leftrightarrow g
breaks: The SC condensate is a composite of electrons, non-relativistic and in a medium with a preferred frame; the electroweak condensate is (as far as known) elementary and Lorentz invariant, and its gauge group is non-abelian.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: Anomaly inflow and bulk-boundary correspondence
summary: Gapless boundary modes of topological phases carry 't Hooft anomalies that are cancelled by inflow from the bulk topological response (Callan-Harvey), so the classification of topological matter is a classification of anomalies.
sources: Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)

name: Axion electrodynamics in topological magnets
summary: The theta angle of a TI plays the role of the axion field; in magnetic TIs theta can fluctuate, giving a dynamical 'axion quasiparticle' whose coupling to E.B mirrors the QCD axion's photon coupling and has been proposed for dark-matter detection.
map: \mathcal L=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi^2}\theta(\mathbf x,t)\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\ \leftrightarrow\ -\frac{g_{a\gamma\gamma}}{4}aF\tilde F,\ \theta\leftrightarrow a/f_a
breaks: The condensed-matter theta is an emergent, lattice-scale field with meV dynamics and no shift symmetry from a QCD anomaly; it cannot solve strong CP or be dark matter itself.
sources: Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)

name: Chiral (ABJ) anomaly in Weyl semimetals
summary: Parallel E and B pump electrons between Weyl nodes of opposite chirality exactly as the Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly; the result is a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance.
sources: Nielsen & Ninomiya (1983). "The Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly and Weyl fermions in a crystal". *Phys. Lett. B* 130, 389. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0)
Son & Spivak (2013). "Chiral Anomaly and Classical Negative Magnetoresistance of Weyl Metals". *Phys. Rev. B* 88, 104412. [arXiv:1206.1627](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.1627)
Adler (1969). "Axial-Vector Vertex in Spinor Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 177, 2426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426)

name: Graphene's massless 2+1D Dirac fermions
summary: Near the K points graphene's tight-binding bands obey the massless 2+1D Dirac equation with c replaced by v_F~c/300 and spin replaced by sublattice pseudospin, giving Klein tunnelling, a half-integer Hall sequence and optical absorption pi*alpha.
map: H=\hbar v_F\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k\ \leftrightarrow\ H_D=c\,\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf p;\ \alpha_g=\frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon\hbar v_F}\approx2.2,\ T=1-\pi\alpha
breaks: Lorentz invariance is only emergent at low energy; the Coulomb interaction is instantaneous (it travels at c, not v_F), so interacting graphene is not a relativistic QFT; valleys double the fermion count.
sources: Novoselov et al. (2005). "Two-dimensional gas of massless Dirac fermions in graphene". *Nature* 438, 197. [arXiv:cond-mat/0509330](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0509330)
Castro Neto et al. (2009). "The electronic properties of graphene". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 109. [arXiv:0709.1163](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1163)
Nair et al. (2008). "Fine Structure Constant Defines Visual Transparency of Graphene". *Science* 320, 1308. [doi:10.1126/science.1156965](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1156965)

name: Weyl equation realized in TaAs
summary: Weyl semimetals host quasiparticles obeying the two-component Weyl equation that elementary physics never confirmed (neutrinos turned out massive); each node is a monopole of Berry curvature with chirality +-1.
breaks: Solid-state Weyl nodes can be tilted (type II), anisotropic and offset in energy, since there is no Lorentz symmetry, and their total number is fixed by the lattice.
sources: Xu et al. (2015). "Discovery of a Weyl fermion semimetal and topological Fermi arcs". *Science* 349, 613. [arXiv:1502.03807](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03807)
Armitage, Mele & Vishwanath (2018). "Weyl and Dirac semimetals in three-dimensional solids". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 90, 015001. [arXiv:1705.01111](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01111)

name: Nielsen-Ninomiya doubling forces paired Weyl nodes
summary: The no-go theorem that lattice chiral fermions come in pairs of opposite chirality is the reason Weyl nodes in a crystal always appear in pairs, and Nielsen and Ninomiya themselves proposed the crystal chiral anomaly.
sources: Nielsen & Ninomiya (1983). "The Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly and Weyl fermions in a crystal". *Phys. Lett. B* 130, 389. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0)

name: Domain-wall fermions are topological boundary states
summary: Kaplan's domain-wall fermions get lattice chiral fermions as zero modes bound to a mass domain wall in one higher dimension, the same Jackiw-Rebbi mechanism that produces protected surface Dirac cones of topological insulators.
map: (i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu-m(s))\psi=0,\ m(s)\to\pm m\ \Rightarrow\ \psi_0\propto e^{-\int^s m(s')ds'}\ (\text{chiral zero mode})
sources: Kaplan (1992). "A Method for simulating chiral fermions on the lattice". *Phys. Lett. B* 288, 342. [arXiv:hep-lat/9206013](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/9206013)
Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)

name: Majorana neutrinos versus Majorana zero modes
summary: Both rest on a self-conjugate fermion psi=psi^c (gamma=gamma-dagger): an elementary Majorana neutrino would violate lepton number in 0nubb, while zero-energy Majorana modes bound to vortices or wire ends obey non-abelian exchange statistics.
breaks: Majorana zero modes are not propagating particles; they are non-abelian anyons bound to defects with no momentum or mass. Several condensed-matter Majorana claims have been retracted or reinterpreted, so evidence there is contested.
sources: Kitaev (2001). "Unpaired Majorana fermions in quantum wires". *Phys.-Usp.* 44, 131. [arXiv:cond-mat/0010440](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0010440)
Beenakker (2013). "Search for Majorana Fermions in Superconductors". *Ann. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 4, 113. [arXiv:1112.1950](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.1950)
Avignone, Elliott & Engel (2008). "Double Beta Decay, Majorana Neutrinos, and Neutrino Mass". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 481. [arXiv:0708.1033](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1033)

name: Topological order as deconfined lattice gauge theory
summary: Z2 topological order (toric code, Z2 spin liquids) is the deconfined phase of Wegner's Z2 lattice gauge theory; anyons are its electric charges and fluxes, and the Wilson-loop perimeter law is the condensed-matter signature of deconfinement.
sources: Wegner (1971). "Duality in Generalized Ising Models and Phase Transitions without Local Order Parameters". *J. Math. Phys.* 12, 2259. [doi:10.1063/1.1665530](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1665530)
Kitaev (2003). "Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons". *Ann. Phys.* 303, 2. [arXiv:quant-ph/9707021](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9707021)
Wen (1990). "Topological orders in rigid states". *Int. J. Mod. Phys. B* 4, 239. [doi:10.1142/S0217979290000139](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0217979290000139)

name: Emergent QED in quantum spin ice
summary: The low-energy theory of a U(1) quantum spin liquid on the pyrochlore lattice is compact U(1) gauge theory: gapless emergent photons with omega ~ k, gapped electric charges (spinons) and magnetic monopoles.
breaks: The emergent speed of light is ~meV scale and lattice-cut off; the emergent fine-structure constant and charges are not tied to QED's, and Lorentz invariance is only approximate.
sources: Hermele, Fisher & Balents (2004). "Pyrochlore photons: The U(1) spin liquid in a S=1/2 three-dimensional frustrated magnet". *Phys. Rev. B* 69, 064404. [arXiv:cond-mat/0305401](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0305401)

name: Could photons and electrons be emergent?
summary: String-net condensation produces emergent U(1) gauge bosons and fermionic charges from local bosonic spins, suggesting the Standard Model's gauge fields and fermions might themselves be emergent.
breaks: No string-net model reproduces chiral fermions, non-abelian SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1), or exact Lorentz invariance; chiral gauge theories resist lattice regularization.
sources: Levin & Wen (2005). "Colloquium: Photons and electrons as emergent phenomena". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 77, 871. [arXiv:cond-mat/0407140](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0407140)

name: Ginzburg-Landau is the abelian Higgs model
summary: Ginzburg-Landau theory is the abelian Higgs model with charge 2e; Abrikosov vortices are Nielsen-Olesen strings and the type-I/II boundary kappa=1/sqrt2 is the BPS point where vortices do not interact.
sources: Nielsen & Olesen (1973). "Vortex-line models for dual strings". *Nucl. Phys. B* 61, 45. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7)

name: Confinement as a dual Meissner effect
summary: If chromomagnetic monopoles condense, chromoelectric flux is squeezed into tubes just as magnetic flux is in a type-II superconductor, giving a linear quark potential with string tension sigma.
breaks: The roles of E and B are swapped, the gauge group is non-abelian, and monopole condensation in QCD is gauge-dependent and unproven analytically.
sources: 't Hooft (1981). "Topology of the gauge condition and new confinement phases in non-Abelian gauge theories". *Nucl. Phys. B* 190, 455. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(81)90442-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90442-9)
Nielsen & Olesen (1973). "Vortex-line models for dual strings". *Nucl. Phys. B* 61, 45. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7)

name: NJL: chiral symmetry breaking modelled on BCS
summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio built dynamical mass generation for nucleons by direct analogy with the BCS gap equation; the massless Goldstone mode of the analogy became the pion, a precursor of QCD chiral symmetry breaking.
sources: Nambu & Jona-Lasinio (1961). "Dynamical Model of Elementary Particles Based on an Analogy with Superconductivity. I". *Phys. Rev.* 122, 345. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.122.345](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.122.345)
Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer (1957). "Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 108, 1175. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175)

name: Color superconductivity in dense quark matter
summary: At high baryon density attractive one-gluon exchange in the color antitriplet channel makes quarks Cooper-pair near the Fermi surface; in the CFL phase the diquark condensate Higgses all eight gluons (color Meissner effect).
sources: Alford, Rajagopal & Wilczek (1999). "Color-flavor locking and chiral symmetry breaking in high density QCD". *Nucl. Phys. B* 537, 443. [arXiv:hep-ph/9804403](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9804403)

name: Higgs amplitude mode in superconductors
summary: The Higgs boson is the amplitude oscillation of the condensate; superconductors have the same mode at energy 2Delta, observed in Raman and terahertz pump-probe experiments.
breaks: In a superconductor the mode sits at the pair-breaking edge and can decay into quasiparticles; its observation needs coupling via a CDW or nonlinear drive since it is Raman- but not dipole-active.
sources: Pekker & Varma (2015). "Amplitude/Higgs Modes in Condensed Matter Physics". *Ann. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 6, 269. [arXiv:1406.2968](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2968)
Matsunaga et al. (2014). "Light-induced collective pseudospin precession resonating with Higgs mode in a superconductor". *Science* 345, 1145. [arXiv:1407.4554](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4554)

name: Goldstone EFT: pions and magnons
summary: Chiral perturbation theory's EFT of Goldstone bosons describes magnons: antiferromagnetic magnons are relativistic-like (O(3) sigma model, omega ~ k) while ferromagnetic ones are type-B Goldstones (omega ~ k^2) that count once per pair of broken generators.
sources: Watanabe & Murayama (2012). "Unified Description of Nambu-Goldstone Bosons without Lorentz Invariance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 251602. [arXiv:1203.0609](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0609)
Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)

name: Quantum critical points as CFTs
summary: Many z=1 quantum critical points are described by conformal field theories (e.g. O(N) Wilson-Fisher in 2+1D) whose finite-T response is universal and Planckian (tau ~ hbar/k_BT); holographic CFTs model strongly coupled transport.
sources: Sachdev & Keimer (2011). "Quantum criticality". *Physics Today* 64, 29. [arXiv:1102.4628](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.4628)

name: FQH edges and wavefunctions from CFT
summary: Edges of quantum Hall states are chiral CFTs, and bulk wavefunctions are CFT conformal blocks: the Laughlin state from a U(1) boson, the Moore-Read Pfaffian from the Ising CFT, whose sigma fields become non-abelian anyons.
sources: Moore & Read (1991). "Nonabelions in the fractional quantum Hall effect". *Nucl. Phys. B* 360, 362. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(91)90407-O](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(91)90407-O)

name: Entanglement scaling reads off the central charge
summary: At a 1+1D critical point the entanglement entropy grows as (c/3) ln L, so DMRG and tensor-network simulations extract CFT central charges and operator dimensions directly from ground states.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2009). "Entanglement entropy and conformal field theory". *J. Phys. A* 42, 504005. [arXiv:0905.4013](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.4013)

name: Chern-Simons theory and the parity anomaly
summary: The quantum Hall response is a Chern-Simons term whose level is the TKNN Chern number; Haldane's honeycomb model realized the 2+1D parity anomaly of a single massive Dirac fermion, the seed of Chern insulators.
sources: Haldane (1988). "Model for a Quantum Hall Effect without Landau Levels: Condensed-Matter Realization of the 'Parity Anomaly'". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 61, 2015. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2015](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2015)

Thouless, Kohmoto, Nightingale & den Nijs (1982). "Quantized Hall Conductance in a Two-Dimensional Periodic Potential". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 405. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405)

name: Quantum-limited amplifiers for axion haloscopes
summary: Cavity haloscopes convert axions to microwave photons in a magnet; SQUID and Josephson parametric amplifiers (and squeezing) bring readout to the quantum limit, setting the scan rate in the micro-eV mass range.
sources: Sikivie (1983). "Experimental Tests of the Invisible Axion". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 51, 1415. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.1415](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.1415)

name: Sub-MeV dark matter scattering into phonons
summary: Below ~MeV, dark-matter momentum transfers match crystal phonon and magnon scales, so detection relies on condensed-matter response functions (dynamic structure factor, dielectric loss) rather than nuclear recoils.
sources: Zurek (2024). "Dark Matter Candidates of a Very Low Mass". *Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 74. [arXiv:2401.03025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03025)

name: Silicon trackers are reverse-biased p-n junctions
summary: Pixel and strip trackers collect electron-hole pairs (3.6 eV per pair in Si) drifting in the depletion region of a reverse-biased p-n junction; radiation damage (displacement defects, type inversion) is semiconductor defect physics.
sources: Particle Data Group (2024). "Review of Particle Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 110, 030001. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001)

name: Cryogenic bolometers for 0nubb
summary: CUORE-type TeO2 crystals at ~10 mK act as calorimeters: the Debye T^3 heat capacity is tiny, so a 2.5 MeV decay raises the temperature measurably and gives keV resolution.
sources: CUORE Collaboration (2020). "Improved Limit on Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay in 130Te with CUORE". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 122501. [arXiv:1912.10966](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.10966)

name: Type-II NbTi magnets bend the LHC beams
summary: The LHC's 8.3 T dipoles use NbTi, a type-II superconductor with strong flux pinning, cooled to 1.9 K in superfluid helium; the beam rigidity and the upper critical field set the reachable energy.

name: Shared Monte Carlo, sign problem and tensor networks
summary: Lattice QCD and correlated-electron numerics share hybrid/determinant Monte Carlo and the fermion sign problem; tensor networks developed for spin chains now simulate lattice gauge theories at finite density and in real time.
map: \langle O\rangle=\frac{\int O\det M\,e^{-S}}{\int\det M\,e^{-S}},\ \det M\ \text{not positive}\Rightarrow\text{sign problem}
sources: Cataldi et al. (2024). "Simulating (2+1)D SU(2) Yang-Mills lattice gauge theory at finite density with tensor networks". [arXiv:2307.09396](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09396)

name: Kondo temperature as dimensional transmutation
summary: The antiferromagnetic Kondo coupling is marginally relevant, so it grows at low energy like an asymptotically free coupling and generates a scale T_K exactly as Lambda_QCD emerges; Wilson's numerical RG solved it.
breaks: Kondo is a 0+1D impurity problem with no gauge field or confinement; the strong-coupling fixed point is a screened singlet (Fermi liquid), not a confined hadron spectrum.
sources: Wilson (1975). "The Renormalization Group: Critical Phenomena and the Kondo Problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 47, 773. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.47.773](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.47.773)

name: DMRG born from the failure of real-space RG
summary: White's DMRG replaced Wilson-style energy truncation by density-matrix truncation, turning real-space renormalization into the most accurate 1D many-body method and the seed of tensor-network RG.
sources: White (1992). "Density matrix formulation for quantum renormalization groups". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 69, 2863. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863)
Schollwöck (2011). "The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states". *Ann. Phys.* 326, 96. [arXiv:1008.3477](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3477)

name: Fermi-surface EFT: BCS as the marginal instability
summary: Treating the Fermi liquid as an EFT with RG scaling toward the Fermi surface shows only forward and BCS couplings survive, and an attractive BCS coupling is marginally relevant and runs to a gap.
sources: Shankar (1994). "Renormalization-group approach to interacting fermions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 66, 129. [arXiv:cond-mat/9307009](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9307009)

name: Emergent supersymmetry at topological boundaries
summary: At the boundary of topological superconductors (or interacting Majorana chains) the critical point can be the tricritical Ising CFT or an N=1 Wess-Zumino theory, with exact emergent supersymmetry between bosonic order parameter and Majorana fermion.
breaks: Supersymmetry is emergent only at fine-tuned criticality and low energy; there is no superpartner spectrum or SUSY breaking scale as in the MSSM.
sources: Grover, Sheng & Vishwanath (2014). "Emergent Space-Time Supersymmetry at the Boundary of a Topological Phase". *Science* 344, 280. [arXiv:1301.7449](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.7449)

name: Running Fermi velocity in graphene
summary: Coulomb interactions renormalize graphene's Fermi velocity logarithmically, like a running coupling, because alpha_g is marginal; suspended graphene shows the predicted log enhancement near the Dirac point.
sources: Elias et al. (2011). "Dirac cones reshaped by interaction effects in suspended graphene". *Nature Phys.* 7, 701. [arXiv:1104.1396](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.1396)

name: Emergent magnetic monopoles in spin ice
summary: Defects violating the two-in-two-out ice rule behave as deconfined magnetic charges with a Coulomb interaction, a laboratory analogue of the magnetic monopoles predicted by grand unification.
breaks: Spin-ice monopoles are sources of H (div B = 0 still holds), their charge is not Dirac-quantized, and they are classical lattice defects rather than 't Hooft-Polyakov solitons of a broken gauge group.
sources: Castelnovo, Moessner & Sondhi (2008). "Magnetic monopoles in spin ice". *Nature* 451, 42. [arXiv:0710.5515](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5515)

name: Phase slips and macroscopic tunnelling as instantons
summary: The escape of a current-biased Josephson phase from a tilted-washboard well is a Euclidean bounce, computed with the same instanton methods as false-vacuum decay; dissipation enters through a Caldeira-Leggett bath.
sources: Coleman (1977). "Fate of the false vacuum: Semiclassical theory". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2929. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2929](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2929)

name: Hedgehogs, strings and the Kibble mechanism
summary: Point and line defects in nematics are classified by the same homotopy groups as GUT monopoles and cosmic strings, and quenches through the isotropic-nematic transition test Kibble's defect-formation scenario.
breaks: Nematic defects have no gauge field, energy that scales with system size, and dissipative rather than relativistic dynamics.
sources: Chuang, Durrer, Turok & Yurke (1991). "Cosmology in the Laboratory: Defect Dynamics in Liquid Crystals". *Science* 251, 1336. [doi:10.1126/science.251.4999.1336](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.251.4999.1336)

name: Boundary CFT solves the multichannel Kondo problem
summary: Affleck and Ludwig treated the impurity as a conformal boundary condition of a 1+1D chiral CFT, obtaining the non-Fermi-liquid exponents and residual entropy of the overscreened multichannel Kondo fixed point.
sources: Affleck & Ludwig (1991). "Critical theory of overscreened Kondo fixed points". *Nucl. Phys. B* 360, 641. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(91)90419-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(91)90419-X)

name: Berry connection as a gauge field on the Brillouin zone
summary: The Berry connection is a U(1) (or, for degenerate bands, Wilczek-Zee non-abelian) gauge field over momentum space; Chern numbers are its first Chern class, the same topology as monopole and instanton charges.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)
Wilczek & Zee (1984). "Appearance of Gauge Structure in Simple Dynamical Systems". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 2111. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111)

name: Composite Higgs and top condensation from BCS
summary: Technicolor and top-quark condensation replace the elementary Higgs by a fermion-pair condensate formed by a gap equation, the BCS template (one author is Bardeen of BCS); the Higgs would be composite.
sources: Bardeen, Hill & Lindner (1990). "Minimal dynamical symmetry breaking of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 41, 1647. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.41.1647](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.41.1647)

name: Emergent gauge fields in the doped Mott insulator
summary: Slave-particle (parton) descriptions of the cuprates split the electron into spinons and holons coupled by an emergent U(1) or SU(2) gauge field, importing gauge-theory confinement and Higgs phases into high-Tc theory.
map: c_{i\sigma}=b_i^\dagger f_{i\sigma},\ \sum_\sigma f^\dagger f+b^\dagger b=1\ (\text{gauge constraint})
sources: Lee, Nagaosa & Wen (2006). "Doping a Mott insulator: Physics of high-temperature superconductivity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 78, 17. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410445](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410445)
